solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Beginner's brief worked out in area is right

parts.note: brief means curt, short in manner

indicators.note: worked out suggests the letters have been reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone says a short piece of work produced in some region is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginner's' reads as a possessive, but the 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay; 'worked out' yields AINRAISER.
explanation.definitionFit: A short opening piece staged before the main play is the thing that begins the evening, hence a beginner.

clue.text: Reportedly down wines in historic coastal locations

indicators.note: reportedly says we go by what is heard, not what is written

parts.note: to down is to sink a drink, and port wines are ports, so sink ports

explanation.surface: Drinkers are said to knock back wine in old seaside towns.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cinque Ports are a group of historic towns on England's south-east coast, Hastings and Dover among them; 'Cinque' is said 'sink'.
explanation.definitionFit: The group of medieval harbour towns in Kent and Sussex are historic places on the coast.

clue.text: Robert originally along with Dorothy ultimately in mood for it?

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the name Robert

parts.note: along with means and

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the name Dorothy

explanation.surface: Robert and Dorothy, it seems, are feeling amorous together.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the mood for it, with 'it' as a coy word for sex, is being lustful or frisky.

clue.text: Dangerous atmosphere when lawyer enters seeking politician

indicators.note: enters means the lawyer goes into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: seeking something is going after it
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician
DA, District Attorney, is an American lawyer

explanation.surface: A lawyer walks in on a tense scene while pursuing a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: The poisonous gas left in a mine after an explosion is a deadly atmosphere for miners.

clue.text: Boy upset females in diners

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a boy is a son
hers is the female possessive, standing for females

explanation.surface: A boy has knocked over some women in a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is slang for food, so those who eat it are people having a meal.

clue.text: Picture ball of fire, oddly disappearing

indicators.note: the letters in odd positions vanish, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A photo of a fireball fades strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: Picture means a film here: Alfie is a 1966 British film starring Michael Caine.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is a cinema film, and this is the title of a famous one.

clue.text: Few top his slogans?

parts.note: read as a cryptic description: few people put messages higher than this person, who writes advertising slogans across the heavens

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests rare praise for an ad man; really his slogans are literally up top, in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot trailing smoke to spell messages overhead writes slogans that hardly anyone can place higher.

clue.text: Publish score at Lord's

definitions.meaning: to print or carry a story in a newspaper
Lord's is the London cricket ground, and a batsman's score is made in single scoring units

explanation.surface: Print the cricket result from the famous London ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper prints a story, and a cricketer scores one point by running between the wickets.

clue.text: Clergyman dropping off Conservative shortly

indicators.note: dropping off means a letter is shed from the word

parts.note: a canon is a clergyman attached to a cathedral

explanation.surface: A cleric nods off; a Tory will follow soon.
explanation.definitionFit: The old word for soon or presently, as in 'I'll be there in a while'.

clue.text: Trying time in Paris is following creation of fiction?

parts.note: est is French for is
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
making things up is lying

explanation.surface: A wearisome stretch in the French capital follows writing a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trying' looks like an adjective meaning tiresome; it is the verb sense, putting something through a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a new aircraft up to check its performance is trying it out in the air.

clue.text: Neither taxed nor tasked?

parts.note: free of duty in both senses: no customs charge and no obligation to work

explanation.walkthrough: Duty is both a tax on goods and a task one must do; being free of it covers both.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods bought at airport shops escape customs charges, and someone off work has no obligations.

clue.text: Improve quality of garden Richelieu used to some extent

indicators.note: used to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cardinal's garden is used partly to make it better.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something richer or better is to upgrade its quality, as soil is fertilised.

clue.text: Song set he cannot fancy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornate, a sign the letters are dressed up anew

explanation.surface: A man cannot like a set of songs.
explanation.definitionFit: A short French song, a little chanson, is a kind of song.

clue.text: Telescopes, initially scarce, procured? Yes — getting used by girls

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of each of the four words that follow

parts.note: lasses are girls

explanation.surface: Rare telescopes are acquired and used by young women.
explanation.definitionFit: Small hand-held telescopes, the kind sailors carried, are known by this old name.

clue.text: Old governor's rule, not the first, blocking legwear item

indicators.note: blocking means the trimmed word sits inside the other, stopping it up

parts.note: a gaiter is a covering for the lower leg

indicators.note: not the first says the word rule loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: An old governor's rule is in force, though he isn't the first in his gaiters.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'governor' stands for 'is'; 'not the first' leaves ULE, which 'blocking' places within the legwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nazi regional party leader held power over a district, an historical kind of governor.

clue.text: Hope surer possibly when he appears?

definitions.text: Hope surer possibly when he appears?

indicators.note: possibly suggests these letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Hope grows more certain when the hero turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: hope rises when a caped saviour arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: A caped crime-fighter's arrival makes rescue look more certain to those in peril.

clue.text: Recalled somewhere to sell vehicle

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a mart is a market, a place to sell

explanation.surface: A dealership has recalled a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A streetcar running on rails through a city is a public transport vehicle.

clue.text: German lady reveals deception after loss of diamonds

indicators.note: after loss of says a letter has been taken away from the word

parts.note: fraud is deception
D is the abbreviation for diamonds, the card suit

explanation.surface: A German woman uncovers a swindle after her jewels go missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Frau is the German word for a married woman or wife, so a German lady.

clue.text: Soldier dropping scraps, you say? Rewording found

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: you say means the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a cloth that frays drops threads and scraps

explanation.surface: A soldier is found dropping bits of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Restating something in other words is a restatement of the original text.

clue.text: Alter position of concrete sign after son leaves

parts.note: concrete means real, actual

indicators.note: leaves says the letter departs from the word

explanation.surface: Move a cement sign once the boy has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift something into a new line or arrangement is to change its placement.

clue.text: When cold finish move up

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
the finish is the end

explanation.surface: Once the cold spell ends, go upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb or rise is to go higher.

clue.text: Nobleman's praise welcoming clubs is brought up

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means raised, read from the bottom upwards
welcoming means taking another letter inside

parts.note: to laud is to praise
C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit

explanation.surface: A lord's acclaim, taking in golf clubs, is raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welcoming' puts C inside LAUD to give LACUD; 'brought up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducal means belonging to a duke, so it describes what is a nobleman's.

clue.text: The writer's taken in by a sidekick — bitterness results

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside the other pieces

parts.note: a crony is a close companion
the writer is the setter, so 'the writer is' becomes I'M

explanation.surface: The author is fooled by a partner, and resentment follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrimony is harsh, angry ill-feeling, a synonym for rancour.

clue.text: Officer has name for judge in estate

indicators.note: for means one letter is put in place of another

parts.note: a major is an army officer

explanation.surface: An officer names a judge to sit in a country house.
explanation.definitionFit: A landed country house with its grounds is a lord's estate.

clue.text: Safeguarding investigator, note, in course of show

indicators.note: in course of means within, partway through the other word

parts.note: to prove is to show to be true
tec is short for detective
ti is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A detective appears partway through a broadcast about security.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping something from harm is shielding it, the adjective's sense here.

clue.text: Tease, when bachelor's married, is borderline?

indicators.note: when the bachelor's married, one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: to rib is to tease

explanation.surface: Is teasing a newly wed former bachelor near the edge?
explanation.definitionFit: A rim is the edge or outer border of something, a line round it.

clue.text: Brief letter of refusal, extremely trite

parts.note: no is a refusal

indicators.note: extremely picks the two extreme letters of the word trite

explanation.surface: A short message turning someone down, and very banal.
explanation.definitionFit: A short informal written message is a memo or a quick line to someone.

clue.text: More iron and manly, bowled over actress

indicators.note: bowled over means knocked flat, so the letters are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A film star is overwhelmed by a tougher, more macho man.
explanation.definitionFit: She was the famous Hollywood film star of the 1950s, so an example of an actress.
